nodes.statement: Any Whittaker module V of type psi that admits a central character chi:\ Z(g)rightarrow C is a quotient of a universal module Y_chi,psi=U(g)otimes_Z(g)U(n)Cw_chi,psi, where Z(g)U(n)=Z(g)otimes U(n) acts on the 1-dimensional space Cw_chi,psi by chiotimespsi. Such modules are always simple if psi is non-singular, but need not be simple for singular psi. By the above corollary, the dimension of hboxWh\,V is bounded by the length of Y_chi,psi. Such lengths have been computed by Milivci\'c and Soergel using Kazhdan-Lusztig theory.
nodes.raw_latex:
{\em 
  Any Whittaker module $V$ of type $\psi$ that admits a central character $\chi:\ Z(\mathfrak{g)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is a quotient of a universal module
  $$\mathcal{Y}_{\chi,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{g)\otimes_{Z(\mathfrak{g)U(\mathfrak{n})}\mathbb{C}w_{\chi,\psi},$$
  where $Z(\mathfrak{g)U(\mathfrak{n})=Z(\mathfrak{g)\otimes U(\mathfrak{n})$ acts on the $1$-dimensional space $\mathbb{C}w_{\chi,\psi}$ by $\chi\otimes\psi$.  Such modules are always simple if $\psi$ is non-singular, but need not be simple for singular $\psi$.  By the above corollary, the dimension of $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is bounded by the length of $\mathcal{Y}_{\chi,\psi}$.  Such lengths have been computed by Mili\v{c}i\'c and Soergel \cite{milicic-soergel97} using Kazhdan-Lusztig theory.
  }
nodes.clean_text: Any Whittaker module V of type psi that admits a central character chi:\ Z(g)rightarrow C is a quotient of a universal module Y_chi,psi=U(g)otimes_Z(g)U(n)Cw_chi,psi, where Z(g)U(n)=Z(g)otimes U(n) acts on the 1-dimensional space Cw_chi,psi by chiotimespsi. Such modules are always simple if psi is non-singular, but need not be simple for singular psi. By the above corollary, the dimension of hboxWh\,V is bounded by the length of Y_chi,psi. Such lengths have been computed by Milivci\'c and Soergel using Kazhdan-Lusztig theory.

nodes.name: Whittaker character
nodes.statement: , and let n be the nilradical of the standard Borel b relative to (g,mathfrak h,Delta). A Lie algebra homomorphism psi:\ nrightarrow C is called a Whittaker character; the character psi is em non-singular if it is nonzero on the root spaces g_alpha for all simple roots alphainDelta. An element v of a g-module V is said to be a Whittaker vector of type psi if xv=psi(x)v for all xinn. The space of Whittaker vectors in V will be denoted by hboxWh\,V. Cyclic modules generated by Whittaker vectors of type psi are called em Whittaker modules of type psi and are singular or non-singular, depending on whether psi is singular or non-singular. Each Whittaker module admits a unique Whittaker character, so the notions of singular and non-singular are well defined.
nodes.raw_latex: , and let $\mathfrak{n}$ be the nilradical of the standard Borel $\mathfrak{b}$ relative to $(\mathfrak{g,{\mathfrak h,\Delta)$.  A Lie algebra homomorphism $\psi:\ \mathfrak{n}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is called a {\em Whittaker character}; the character $\psi$ is {\em non-singular} if it is nonzero on the root spaces $\mathfrak{g_\alpha$ for all simple roots $\alpha\in\Delta$.  An element $v$ of a $\mathfrak{g$-module $V$ is said to be a {\em Whittaker vector of type} $\psi$ if $xv=\psi(x)v$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{n}$.  The space of Whittaker vectors in $V$ will be denoted by $\hbox{Wh}\,V$.  Cyclic modules generated by Whittaker vectors of type $\psi$ are called {\em Whittaker modules of type} $\psi$ and are {\em singular} or {\em non-singular}, depending on whether $\psi$ is singular or non-singular.  Each Whittaker module admits a unique Whittaker character, so the notions of singular and non-singular are well defined.
